update.description: Creation of a “centre of expertise” which works with subject matter specialists to expedite the negotiation and acquisition of administrative and alternative data
strategic priorities: Existing data holding are exploited to the greatest extent possible.
New data needs are addressed to the greatest extent possible through administrative and alternative data, with household and business surveys being conducted only when necessary.
The time and effort involved in acquiring administrative and alternative data is significantly reduced

phases.justification: A 'centre of expertise' focused on data acquisition directly supports the initial assessment of data availability and the acquisition process.
Expediting negotiation and acquisition of administrative data directly impacts the collection phase, especially for non-survey sources.
This sub-process involves setting up procedures to receive or extract information from non-survey sources, which the 'centre of expertise' would facilitate.
The actual running of collection for administrative data (e.g., scheduled data provision from partners) would be expedited.

update.description: Pilot projects to enable partners to clean data using AI, prior to its ingestion by Statistics Canada (e.g. Cancer Registry) (2.4)
strategic priorities: The length and response burden of questionnaires is optimised to balance respondent experience, data quality and information needs.

phases.justification: The update explicitly references GSBPM step 2.4, implying potential adjustments or considerations in the design of frames or samples when partners pre-clean data.
Enabling partners to clean data using AI before ingestion would significantly impact the quality of data received, thus influencing data integration by providing cleaner input.
Pre-cleaning data by partners using AI would reduce the need for extensive review and validation by Statistics Canada, shifting some of this work upstream.

update.description: Creation of a “trusted environment” which allows for the ingestion and processing of “risky” data through the use of confidential computing and other emerging technologies
strategic priorities: Confidentiality and privacy of data are ensured in the face of increasingly sensitive data holdings and new techniques for data integration and dissemination.

phases.justification: The creation of a 'trusted environment' affects how data collection is set up, particularly concerning secure channels and confidentiality procedures for acquiring sensitive data.
The ingestion of 'risky' data requires specific loading procedures and security considerations when finalizing collection, which this environment would address.
The 'trusted environment' is explicitly for 'processing' risky data, directly impacting data integration activities that might involve sensitive or complex sources.
Processing of 'risky' data within a trusted environment necessitates specific review and validation protocols to ensure data quality and security are maintained.

update.description: Elimination of duplicative data holdings by ensuring that data ingested and processed in the “trusted environment” becomes the master copy of the data (4.4)
strategic priorities: Data infrastructure is modernized to support the more efficient acquisition, processing and delivery of data and statistical products.

phases.justification: The update explicitly references GSBPM step 4.4, indicating that once data is ingested and processed in the trusted environment, it becomes the master copy at the finalisation of collection.
Making data ingested in the 'trusted environment' the master copy directly impacts how data is integrated, as it prioritizes this source and prevents redundant integration efforts.
Ensuring a single master copy eliminates the need for managing and reconciling multiple data holdings, which simplifies the finalization of data files.

update.description: All data collected and processed by StatCan will be available via the Common Output Data Repository (CODR) (5.8)
strategic priorities: Data infrastructure is modernized to support the more efficient acquisition, processing and delivery of data and statistical products.

phases.justification: The update explicitly references GSBPM step 5.8, indicating that the final data files will be made available through the CODR.
The CODR is essentially an output system that needs to be updated with data and metadata. This sub-process manages such updates.
The availability of data in CODR will influence how dissemination products are created, as they will draw from this central repository.
Ensuring all processed data is in CODR means it must be considered during the design of production systems and workflow, particularly for data flow to dissemination.
Building or reusing dissemination components would need to account for the CODR as the central data repository.

update.description: Establishment of a “centre of expertise” for artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies
strategic priorities: Emerging methods and technologies (e.g. AI, cloud, big data) are used to modernize statistical production.
A culture of innovation is fostered, with investments in experimentation and learning.

phases.justification: AI/ML expertise can be applied to automate classification and coding processes.

AI/ML can be used in advanced analytical techniques to interpret and explain outputs more effectively, or to generate initial drafts.
